name: The Molt Flash (Mass Geneware Reveal Event)
description: Originating in the body-modification communities of Tier 2 and spreading unpredictably across tiers, the Molt Flash is a BCI-coordinated event in which participants simultaneously reveal geneware modifications they have been concealing under clothing, cosmetic overlays, or social habit — tails, sub-dermal bioluminescence, vestigial wings, chromatic skin — in a single public moment of collective exposure. Flashes last between four and twelve minutes and have occurred in corporate transit hubs, Tier 4 commercial plazas, and open the Gray Zone markets with equal frequency. The first documented Molt Flash occurred in 2218 at the Meridian Central Transit Interchange and involved roughly three hundred participants; by 2223 individual Flashes regularly exceeded two thousand. The phenomenon carries a charged political valence around geneware-holder rights but organizers consistently resist formal alignment with any advocacy group.
cultural_impact: The Molt Flash has meaningfully shifted public comfort with visible geneware in mixed-tier spaces, and several corponations have quietly updated their employee appearance policies in response to the public relations risk of being seen suppressing participants.
key_figures: Xiulan Oduya-Ferreira (credited with the first Flash)
story_hooks: A Molt Flash is planned for the headquarters plaza of a corponation that has been lobbying against geneware-holder protections — and the organizers receive an anonymous threat.
A participant in a recent Flash is later found dead; their geneware modifications were not cosmetic, and someone didn't want them seen.
A Tier 5 executive's child participates in a Flash, revealing modifications the family has hidden for years — the political fallout reshapes a corporate succession.
